paper.title: SkillBuffBench: Measuring What Agent Skills Contribute across Harnesses, Models, Skill Access Modes and Memory
paper.abstract: Agent Skills, file-based packages of procedural knowledge that a coding agent can discover and load on demand, are now shipped by every major agent harness, yet the evidence for how much they help comes almost entirely from settings in which the right Skill is hand-picked for the task and the agent starts from a blank slate. Neither holds in deployment, where an agent chooses from whatever library happens to be installed and frequently carries memory from earlier work. We present SkillBuffBench, a benchmark and paired evaluation protocol that treats Skill access as a three-level factor (no Skill, a curated Skill, and automatic invocation from an installed library), crosses it with memory (off and on), with four agent harnesses and with multiple models (the state-of-the-art proprietary models from Anthropic, Google and OpenAI, and the state-of-the-art open-weight models from Chinese providers), every model being run under every harness, and evaluates the result on research tasks contributed by domain experts together with the Skills they use, currently in materials science and biology, with the suite extended on a rolling basis. Every run is marked by a deterministic verifier; uncertainty is reported with a paired, task-level bootstrap; and cost, agent rounds and wall-clock time are reported alongside the score rather than folded into it. This version of the paper describes the design of the benchmark, its evaluation protocol and its current tasks and Skills. The evaluation is in progress: results will be added once the runs are complete, and the task suite, results and analysis will continue to be updated on a rolling basis.

paper.title: FastKernels: Benchmarking GPU Kernel Generation in Production
paper.abstract: LLM-based agents for GPU kernel generation are advancing rapidly, but the benchmarks they optimize against evaluate kernels in isolation, with synthetic inputs and weak baselines, rewarding sandbox speedups that break or vanish in real inference systems. We introduce FastKernels, a benchmark of 384 tasks drawn from 47 representative architectures across 8 categories, whose kernels suffice to reimplement 94.6% (472/499) of HuggingFace Transformers architectures with outputs matching the native implementations. Each task mirrors the interface of the corresponding production module and is scored against the kernels production frameworks ship, and tasks form a compositional hierarchy, from primitives to full models, in which higher-level modules import lower-level ones. Candidates are scored at the kernel level and end to end inside the models they come from, on the production execution path, and MacroEval aggregates calibrated correctness, coverage, and speedup into a leaderboard. Seeding it with five representative agents (6,900 agent-hours), we find that kernel-level speedups of $1.6$-$6.6\times$ shrink to at most $1.25\times$ end to end, only 20% of winning kernel sets run correctly as-is, and kernel-level scores mis-rank agents: Claude Code matches or beats KDA at every level in isolation, yet KDA scores $3\times$ higher end to end. Code is available at https://github.com/Snowflake-AI-Research/fastkernels.

paper.title: Sage S2.1 Flash Technical Report
paper.abstract: We introduce Sage S1.5 Flash, a 320-billion-parameter general-purpose mixture-of-experts model designed to reason over scientific evidence and act in interactive environments. Sage Sci-Perception uses dedicated encoders for molecular graphs and biological sequences and represents spectra as ordered patches of measurements. Modality-specific projectors map these representations into the input space of a shared backbone, which processes them alongside text and images. To develop the model's agent capabilities, we construct verifiable environments for tool use, search, and coding, as well as specialized workflows involving machine learning experiments and scientific software. Task completion is checked against execution results, changes in environment state, or submitted artifacts. We evaluate Sage S1.5 Flash on 33 benchmarks across seven domains. In the primary comparison against five baselines, it ranks first on OfficeQA Pro (72.2), MLE-bench Lite (90.3 HumanRank), Harvey LAB, and SpreadsheetBench~2, and second on OSWorld-Verified (85.2), WebArena-Verified (67.6), and DeepResearch Bench~II (54.2). These results show particular strengths in using documentary evidence, producing verifiable workbooks, and carrying out machine learning tasks, alongside competitive performance in desktop and browser workflows that require the model to act on visual feedback.
